profile.summary: MassFormer predicts the tandem mass spectrum (MS/MS) of a small molecule from its structure. It takes a molecule (as SMILES) plus spectrum metadata such as precursor adduct and collision energy, and outputs a binned spectrum. Predicted spectra can be used to identify compounds by comparing them with measured spectra.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: introduction; arXiv 2111.04824v3 Section 2.1 and abstract

summary_quotes.text: This is the original implementation of MassFormer, a graph transformer for small molecule MS/MS prediction.
This chemical representation is combined with spectrum metadata and passed to an MLP that makes a prediction in the form of a sparse positive vector.
we show that it can match or exceed existing prediction-based methods on two spectrum identification tasks.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: MassFormer adapts the Graphormer graph transformer. Node and edge embeddings are taken from the molecular graph, the graph transformer models relationships between all atoms, and a readout gives one embedding for the molecule. This embedding is combined with metadata (precursor adduct, collision energy) and passed to an MLP that outputs a binned spectrum. The transformer and input embeddings are initialised from a Graphormer model pre-trained on PCQM4Mv2 (about 4 million molecular graphs with simulated HOMO-LUMO gaps), then the whole model is fine-tuned on MS/MS spectra.

quotes.text: MassFormer uses a graph transformer architecture to model long-distance relationships between atoms in the molecule.
Our approach adapts the Graphormer [37] architecture
The input embedding and graph transformer parameters are initialized from a Graphormer model [37] that was pre-trained on a large chemical dataset
was originally trained on the PCQM4Mv2 dataset [67, 71], a large dataset of approximately 4 million 2D molecular graphs and their Density Functional Theory (DFT) simulated HOMO-LUMO energy gap.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The repository is the original implementation that accompanies the arXiv preprint (three versions; v3 dated 1 May 2023) and the Nature Machine Intelligence paper. The models in the manuscript were trained on the NIST 2020 MS/MS library, and NIST does not allow their parameters to be redistributed, so no manuscript checkpoints are released. The one public checkpoint is a demo model trained on MoNA with an InChIKey split (checkpoints/demo.pkl, from Zenodo record 8399738). Configs are provided to retrain on NIST and MoNA, including models at 1.0 Da and 0.1 Da bin sizes. A result should state the config file, the training data and whether NIST was used.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Supervised spectrum predictor (molecule to MS/MS spectrum) built on a pre-trained graph transformer.

quotes.text: a graph transformer for small molecule MS/MS prediction
The transformer module is initialized with parameters obtained through a chemical pre-training task, then fine-tuned on spectral data.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Graphormer-based graph transformer with a readout embedding, concatenated with spectrum metadata and fed to an MLP that predicts a binned spectrum; the README's example evaluation config (mona_scaffold) uses graphormer_base with a NEIMS-type feed-forward head and bidirectional prediction.

diagram.caption: The graph transformer is initialised from a pre-trained Graphormer and fine-tuned with the MLP on MS/MS data.

quotes.text: Extraction of node and edge embeddings from the molecular graph, application of the graph transformer, extraction of the chemical embedding from the readout node, addition of spectral metadata (such as collision energy), and prediction of the binned spectrum.

run_guide.summary: Install the GPU environment, download the demo data and checkpoint, run the demo evaluation and then predict spectra for the example SMILES file.
prerequisites: For the GPU route, a GPU compatible with CUDA 11.3 and at least 12 GB VRAM is recommended; a CPU environment is also documented.
wget, used by the download script; the demo data and checkpoint come from Zenodo record 8399738.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/Roestlab/massformer.git
cd massformer
git checkout --detach 8eeb29b6defbc445f0e00816d122291ba471444d
steps.explanation: Clone the repository and pin the reviewed commit. The clone and checkout lines are added by Rewire; the README starts from the repository root.

quotes.text: Enter the root directory and run the following commands:

steps.title: Create the environment
steps.shell:
conda create -n MF-GPU -y
conda activate MF-GPU
conda install python=3.8 -y
pip install -r env/requirements-gpu.txt --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu113 -f https://data.pyg.org/whl/torch-1.12.1+cu113.html -f https://data.dgl.ai/wheels/repo.html
pip install -I -e .
steps.explanation: GPU environment as the README gives it. For CPU only, use the MF-CPU commands and env/requirements-cpu.txt from the README instead.

quotes.text: conda create -n MF-GPU -y conda activate MF-GPU conda install python=3.8 -y

steps.title: Run the demo
steps.explanation: Loads the demo checkpoint and evaluates on a held-out MoNA subset. Use -d -1 for CPU.

quotes.text: python scripts/run_train_eval.py -c config/demo/demo_eval.yml -w off -d 0

steps.title: Predict spectra for SMILES
steps.explanation: Predicts spectra for the example SMILES file and writes a CSV.
steps.source_locator: README.md: Using a Pretrained Model to Make Predictions

quotes.text: python scripts/run_inference.py -c config/demo/demo_eval.yml -s predictions/example_smiles.csv -o predictions/example_predictions.csv -d 0

outputs: The demo prints dataset counts, the parameter counts and a test loss (mol_loss_obj_mean = 0.4836 in the README's expected output).
The inference step writes predictions/example_predictions.csv, with 11 columns including predicted spectra; unparseable SMILES are omitted.
